predecessors.name: Tang dynasty
predecessors.text: the Zhenhai Military Governorate (Hangzhou) and the prefectures the Qian family took from 886: Zhejiang, Shanghai and southern Jiangsu

successors.name: Song dynasty (Northern and Southern Song)
successors.text: Zhejiang, Shanghai, southern Jiangsu and Fuzhou: 13 prefectures given up by Qian Chu in 978

ledger.x: 907: Qian Liu proclaims Wuyue at Hangzhou.
946: Wuyue takes Fuzhou, the Min capital.
978: Qian Chu surrenders Wuyue to the Song.

wars.name: Wuyue-Yang Wu border wars
wars.outcome: Intermittent fighting over border cities after Dong Chang's fall in 896; Huainan attacked Hangzhou in 901-902 and withdrew; in 919 Qian Chuanguan won at Langshan but lost at Wuxi.

wars.name: Wuyue campaign against Changzhou
wars.outcome: 'In 956 armies were sent capture Changzhou'; Changzhou was besieged but the Wuyue army suffered heavy losses against a Southern Tang relief force.

wars.name: Song absorption of Wuyue
wars.outcome: Qian Chu 'facing annihilation by northern imperial troops' pledged allegiance and surrendered his territories in 978 without a recorded battle.

certainty.note: No treaty line is recorded; the frontier with Yang Wu, then the Southern Tang, along the Taihu lowland and the Huainan hills is approximate, and Fuzhou in 946-949 is a coastal enclave known by its prefecture only.

sources.title: Five Dynasties and Ten Kingdoms period
